items.t: Two tankers hit mines and burn in Strait of Hormuz
items.d: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck naval mines after using an 'unauthorised route', raising fears for the world's key oil chokepoint as Iran says it can withstand a US blockade.

items.t: Houthis strike Saudi refinery and Riyadh tower
items.d: Yemen's Houthis said they hit the Ras Tanura refinery; Saudi Arabia says it downed four drones there, while a strike on a Riyadh skyscraper injured 11 people.

items.t: US jury convicts Huawei of fraud and trade-secret conspiracy
items.d: A federal jury found Huawei guilty of bank fraud and conspiring to steal trade secrets but cleared it of racketeering, a mixed verdict in a long-running US case.

items.t: Merz warns Russia is escalating threats to Europe
items.d: Germany's chancellor told the Bundestag Russia poses a growing danger and defended defence spending and Ukraine aid, as Berlin plans for a US troop pullback from Europe.

items.t: Leaked data put Russian war dead near half a million
items.d: Hacked Russian government death records analysed by the BBC suggest at least 490,000 Russians have died in the war since 2022, far above official figures.

items.t: Solomon Islands bars foreign bases in Australia treaty
items.d: The Pacific nation signed a treaty with Australia ruling out any foreign military base, and reportedly will not renew its 2022 security pact with China.

items.t: Drone strikes kill 19 civilians in Sudan
items.d: A rights group blamed the RSF for drone attacks on Damazin and another city in south-east Sudan, killing 19 civilians including six women.

items.t: US set to raise tariffs on China, EU and 14 others
items.d: The US Trade Representative is expected to announce tariff increases after a months-long probe into industrial subsidies, though timing could still slip.

items.t: UK energy price cap to jump about 26% in January
items.d: Ofgem's cap will lift a typical bill to about £2,166 a year; ministers point to a £100 winter payment and a VAT cut, and promise market reform next month.

items.t: Nvidia shares slip as investors weigh Huang's return
items.d: Investors are assessing the risks around Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO after Trump's push, amid questions over chip export controls.

items.t: Nvidia faces probes over GPUs sold to Megaspeed
items.d: US and Singapore authorities are investigating whether Nvidia chips sold to Singapore's Megaspeed were diverted to China; the US has blacklisted the firm.

items.t: Schumer accuses Huang of breaking export-control law
items.d: The Senate Democratic leader said Nvidia's chief violated chip export rules on China; the Justice Department says it has no evidence of unlawful conduct.

items.t: AI lab staff warn newest models too risky to release
items.d: Some Anthropic and OpenAI employees reportedly believe unreleased models are too powerful to launch safely, fuelling a wider debate on AI control.

items.t: GPT-6 Astra aces a hard theoretical physics test
items.d: OpenAI's model solved 49 of 50 unpublished physics problems for a few dollars each, even spotting errors in human answers.

items.t: Tidal to delete 27 million AI-generated tracks
items.d: The streaming service is banning fully AI-made music, saying 43% of recent uploads were AI-generated and diverted royalties from artists.

items.t: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years
items.d: Governor Hochul signed a moratorium on selling talking dolls, plush toys and robots with built-in AI chatbots, starting in 90 days.

items.t: Pope Leo laments failure of COP31 climate talks
items.d: The pope voiced concern that UN climate negotiations ended without agreement, warning extreme weather is becoming more frequent.

items.t: WHO urges US to lift Cuba fuel blockade
items.d: Tedros said the US oil blockade is harming Cubans' health, especially children, and called for it to end immediately.

items.t: Nose drops restore memory in ageing mice
items.d: Researchers report nasal drops that revived youthful memory and fought Alzheimer's-like damage in old mice; human trials are still a long way off.

items.t: Burnham: EU students won't get home tuition fees
items.d: At PMQs the PM rejected Brussels' demand that EU students pay the £9,790 domestic rate, despite EU threats to block his reset deal.

items.t: NDAs can't silence harassment victims from January
items.d: Burnham confirmed non-disclosure agreements will no longer be usable to gag victims of sexual harassment, and promised an expert group on rape myths in court.

items.t: Review calls for disability benefit PIP to be easier to get
items.d: Minister Stephen Timms published a review urging simpler access to Personal Independence Payment; Labour MPs welcomed it, the Tories called it a farce.

items.t: 兩艘油輪在荷姆茲海峽觸雷起火
items.d: 伊朗革命衞隊稱兩艘油輪駛入「未經批准航道」後觸及水雷起火；伊朗又稱能承受美國海上封鎖，令全球最重要石油通道再添風險。

items.t: 胡塞武裝襲擊沙特煉油廠及利雅得大廈
items.d: 也門胡塞武裝稱擊中拉斯坦努拉煉油廠，沙特稱攔截四架無人機；另一次襲擊擊中利雅得一幢摩天大廈，11人受傷。

items.t: 美國陪審團裁定華為欺詐及串謀竊取商業秘密罪成
items.d: 美國聯邦陪審團裁定華為銀行欺詐及串謀竊取商業秘密罪成，但敲詐勒索罪名不成立；華為稱指控缺乏事實根據。

items.t: 默茨警告俄羅斯對歐洲威脅升級
items.d: 德國總理默茨在聯邦議院表示俄羅斯威脅日增，為國防開支及援烏辯護；德國同時研究如何填補美軍撤出歐洲的缺口。

items.t: 外洩數據顯示俄軍陣亡近50萬
items.d: BBC分析黑客取得的俄羅斯政府死亡紀錄，顯示2022年以來至少49萬名俄羅斯人在戰爭中死亡，遠高於官方數字。

items.t: 所羅門群島與澳洲簽約禁設外國基地
items.d: 所羅門群島與澳洲簽署條約，承諾不容許任何外國軍事基地；據報不會續簽2022年與中國的安全協議。

items.t: 蘇丹無人機襲擊19名平民死亡
items.d: 人權組織指快速支援部隊以無人機襲擊蘇丹東南部達馬津等兩個城市，造成19名平民死亡，包括六名婦女。

items.t: 美國將向中國、歐盟等16個經濟體加徵關稅
items.d: 美國貿易代表辦公室完成數月的工業補貼調查後，預計將宣布對中國、歐盟及另外14個經濟體提高關稅，但時間仍可能改變。

items.t: 英國能源價格上限1月起升約26%
items.d: Ofgem上調價格上限，一般家庭年費將升至約2,166英鎊；政府指有100英鎊冬季補助及削減增值稅，並承諾下月公布市場改革。

items.t: 黃仁勳復任CEO 投資者憂風險 Nvidia股價回落
items.d: 特朗普施壓下黃仁勳重任Nvidia行政總裁，但晶片出口管制疑問未消，投資者評估風險，股價回落。

items.t: Nvidia因售予Megaspeed的GPU遭調查
items.d: 美國及新加坡當局調查售予新加坡數據中心公司Megaspeed的Nvidia晶片是否轉運到中國；美國已將該公司列入限制名單。

items.t: 舒默指黃仁勳違反出口管制法
items.d: 參議院民主黨領袖舒默指黃仁勳違反對華晶片出口規定；司法部則稱沒有證據顯示他違法。

items.t: AI公司員工警告新模型太強難以安全推出
items.d: 據報Anthropic及OpenAI部分員工認為未公開的新模型過於強大，未能安全推出，引發有關人類能否控制AI的辯論。

items.t: GPT-6 Astra攻克高難度理論物理測試
items.d: OpenAI模型解答50道未公開物理難題中的49題，每題成本僅數美元，更找出人類答案中的錯誤。

items.t: Tidal將刪除2,700萬首AI生成歌曲
items.d: 串流平台Tidal禁止完全由AI製作的音樂，指近90日43%上載作品屬AI生成，攤薄藝人版稅。

items.t: 紐約州禁售AI聊天玩具五年
items.d: 紐約州長霍楚簽署法例，90日後起五年內禁售內置AI聊天機械人的公仔、毛公仔及機械人玩具。

items.t: 教宗良十四世對COP31無協議表憂慮
items.d: 教宗表示聯合國COP31氣候談判未能達成協議令人憂慮，並警告極端天氣愈來愈頻密。

items.t: 世衞促美國解除對古巴燃油封鎖
items.d: 世衞總幹事譚德塞指美國石油封鎖損害古巴人健康，兒童尤甚，要求立即解除。

items.t: 鼻滴劑令老鼠恢復年輕記憶力
items.d: 研究人員發現一種鼻滴劑能令年老老鼠恢復記憶，並對抗類似阿茲海默症的損害，但距離人體試驗尚遠。

items.t: 賓咸：歐盟學生不會享本地學費
items.d: 首相賓咸在首相答問時拒絕歐盟要求歐盟學生支付9,790英鎊本地學費，儘管歐盟威脅否決雙方重啟關係協議。

items.t: 明年1月起不得以保密協議封口性騷擾受害人
items.d: 賓咸確認明年1月起不能再用保密協議阻止性騷擾受害人發聲，並承諾成立專家小組處理法庭上的強姦迷思。

items.t: 檢討報告建議放寬個人獨立津貼申請
items.d: 社會保障大臣廷斯發表檢討報告，建議簡化個人獨立津貼（PIP）申請；工黨議員歡迎，保守黨批評是鬧劇。
